source: NCERT Class X, Understanding Economic Development, Economics Ch. 3.

sections.heading: 1. Money as a Medium of Exchange
points: **Barter** needs a **double coincidence of wants** (both parties must want what the other has) — inefficient.
**Money** removes this problem — it acts as a **medium of exchange**; a person can sell goods for money and buy anything with it.
Modern forms of money: **currency (coins/notes)** — the RBI issues notes on behalf of the government; and **deposits with banks** (demand deposits, cheques).

sections.heading: 2. Banks and Credit
points: Banks keep a small part of deposits as **cash** (to pay depositors on demand) and **lend the rest** — the main source of bank income is the **difference between interest charged on loans and interest paid on deposits**.
**Credit (loan)** = an agreement where the lender supplies money/goods in return for a promise of future repayment.

**Terms of credit**: interest rate, **collateral**, documentation and mode of repayment; **collateral** = an asset (land, building, vehicle, deposits) the borrower owns, used as a guarantee to the lender.

sections.heading: 3. Two Faces of Credit — Formal and Informal
points: Credit can **help** (e.g. a farmer or trader who profits) or **trap** in a **debt-trap** (e.g. crop failure → cannot repay → sells land).
**Formal sector loans** — banks and cooperatives; supervised by the **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)**; charge **lower interest**.
**Informal sector loans** — moneylenders, traders, employers, relatives; **no supervision, very high interest**, often exploitative.
The **poor depend more on the informal sector** — a key problem; expanding **formal credit** to all is essential.

sections.heading: 4. Self-Help Groups and the Poor
points: **Self-Help Groups (SHGs)** — small groups (usually 15–20 members, mostly women) that pool **savings**; members can take small loans from the group at reasonable interest.
SHGs help the poor get **collateral-free loans**, become self-reliant, and are the building blocks of organisation; banks lend to the group.
**Grameen Bank of Bangladesh (Muhammad Yunus)** is a famous model of micro-credit for the poor.

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Barter needs double coincidence of wants; money removes it.
RBI issues currency notes (on behalf of the government).
Collateral = asset used as guarantee for a loan.
Formal loans = banks/cooperatives (RBI-supervised, low interest); informal = moneylenders (high interest).
SHGs = pooled savings, collateral-free small loans (mostly women); Grameen Bank (Yunus, Bangladesh).

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: **Currency notes are issued by the RBI** (on behalf of the central government).
**Collateral** is a **guarantee/asset**, not the loan itself.
**Formal-sector credit is supervised by the RBI**; informal is not.
**SHGs** provide **collateral-free** loans and are mostly run by **women**.
